• 2026-11-22

    Hacked target: Endurance Bridge

    Description of the event: Fusionist’s Endurance Bridge (ACE cross-chain bridge) was exploited on November 22, 2026. An attacker used privileged minting authority to create large amounts of unbacked ACE tokens on BNB Chain and sold them for approximately $1.04M–$2M, crashing the price. Opportunistic traders then bought the cheap tokens and redeemed them via the bridge for real ACE, draining about $3.7M from the bridge reserves. The project issued a security alert advising users to pause ACE transfers, trading, and bridging on BSC.

    Amount of loss: $ 5,700,000 Attack method: Private Key Leakage

  • 2026-11-21

    Hacked target: Chainflip

    Description of the event: Cross-chain swap protocol Chainflip was attacked on November 21, 2026. The attacker, through a suspected compromise of the aggregate signing key, drained 122.86 BTC, 520.22 ETH, approximately 3.25 million USDC and 758K USDT from its Bitcoin and Ethereum vaults, totaling about $12 million. Some ETH proceeds were quickly sent to Tornado Cash. The project entered full safe mode (disabling deposits, withdrawals and swaps) and offered the attacker a 10% bounty in exchange for returning 90% of the funds.

    Amount of loss: $ 12,000,000 Attack method: Private Key Leak

  • 2026-11-21

    Hacked target: Cyber Bridge

    Description of the event: On November 21, 2026, Cyber’s cross-chain bridge experienced an anomaly: approximately 5.213 million CYBER tokens were unexpectedly minted on Solana, followed shortly by the transfer of the same amount out of the Ethereum lockbox. The attacker sold most of the tokens for about 575 ETH (roughly $968K–$1.1M). The project is investigating and advises users to pause bridge usage and avoid depositing CYBER to exchanges. No migration or signing is required. Several exchanges have suspended deposits/withdrawals.

    Amount of loss: $ 1,100,000 Attack method: Unknown

  • 2026-11-21

    Hacked target: Aramid Bridge

    Description of the event: On November 21, 2026, Aramid Bridge’s Base bridge contract was exploited via a signature-replay bug. The attacker reused the same valid signature multiple times to withdraw assets, minting large amounts of unbacked aVOI that were redeemed for real assets. Bridging is paused and Algorand/Voi escrows have been rekeyed. No private keys, multisig, or signer infrastructure were compromised.

    Amount of loss: $ 8500 Attack method: Signature Replay Bug

  • 2026-11-20

    Hacked target: Wagyu (XMR1)

    Description of the event: On November 20, 2026, Wagyu’s wrapped Monero token XMR1 was exploited. An attacker obtained the deployer private key, transferred 5.2 million XMR1 from the deployer wallet, and sold approximately 364,000–370,000 tokens on Hyperliquid for about $13.5 million, causing the price to crash more than 99% from nearly $500 to around $1. The founder blamed a breach at hosting provider 1984.hosting that exposed the key from retained logs of a deleted server, promised personal refunds to affected users, and suspended the service. Native Monero (XMR) was unaffected.

    Amount of loss: $ 13,500,000 Attack method: Private Key Leakage

  • 2026-11-19

    Hacked target: Fluidkey

    Description of the event: Privacy wallet Fluidkey was attacked on November 19, 2026. The attacker exploited vulnerabilities in the third-party logging tool SigNoz to read internal logs, obtain user session tokens, forge transfer requests, and raise limits. Unauthorized transfers were completed when users opened the app and triggered signing, draining approximately $1.6 million from 52 accounts across Ethereum, Base, BNB Chain, Polygon, Optimism, and Arbitrum. Private keys on users’ devices were not compromised. The project paused services and restored them the next day, later releasing a post-mortem.

    Amount of loss: $ 1,600,000 Attack method: Supply Chain Attack

    Hacked target: K3 Capital

    Description of the event: On November 18, 2026, K3 Capital’s sBOLD vault (a yield-bearing ERC-4626 vault built on Liquity V2 Stability Pools) was exploited.   • 2026-11-18

    Hacked target: RNT Lend

    Description of the event: On November 18, 2026, RNT Lend (Reental’s Aave V3 white-label lending market on Polygon) was drained. An authorized admin key was used to upgrade the USDT0 and USDC proxy contracts to malicious code that allowed unrestricted withdrawals. Approximately $954,703–$955,000 in stablecoins was extracted ($454,825 by two MEV bots that front-ran the keyholder, and ~$500,000 by the keyholder who bridged the funds out). About $49.34 million in property tokens were also taken but fully clawed back by Reental within roughly two hours. Stablecoin liquidity was emptied and withdrawals froze.

  • 2026-11-17

    Hacked target: Paytaca

    Description of the event: Self-custodial Bitcoin Cash (BCH) wallet Paytaca suffered backend vulnerability exploits on November 17–18, 2026. Attackers used flaws in its P2P Ramp and other backend systems to generate fraudulent orders and unsolicited payment requests. The team stated the attacks targeted backend infrastructure only; private keys remain solely on users’ devices and are never stored on servers, so fund transfers still require user signatures. User funds and private keys were unaffected. The team is investigating/fixing the issues and advises users to ignore suspicious orders/requests and never sign transactions they did not initiate.

    Amount of loss: 0 Attack method: Backend Vulnerability
